title: The depth of a nonzero finite module over a Noetherian local ring is at most the dimension of its support
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], i.e. a Noetherian commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and let $M\neq0$ be a finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let $\operatorname{Supp}(M)$ be the set of prime ideals $\mathfrak p\subset R$ with $M_{\mathfrak p}\neq0$, where $M_{\mathfrak p}=S^{-1}M$, $S=R\setminus\mathfrak p$, is the localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], and let $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)\in\{0,1,2,\dots\}\cup\{\infty\}$ be the supremum of the integers $n\ge0$ for which there is a chain $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\mathfrak p_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_n$ of prime ideals of $R$ all lying in $\operatorname{Supp}(M)$. Then $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)\ge\operatorname{depth}(M)$, where $\operatorname{depth}(M)=\operatorname{depth}_{\mathfrak m}(M)$ is the depth [def-weil-pbc-depth].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00LK (lemma-bound-depth, lines 17813-17817), proof lines 17819-17835. Tag verified in tags/tags: 00LK,algebra-lemma-bound-depth

proof.text:
($\mathfrak mM
eq M$, so the depth is a supremum over regular sequences.) Since $\mathfrak m$ is the only maximal ideal of $R$, it is the Jacobson radical of $R$; $M$ is finite and $M
eq0$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson] (with $I=\mathfrak m$) $\mathfrak mM
eq M$. Hence case (1) of [def-weil-pbc-depth] applies: $\operatorname{depth}(M)$ is the supremum of the lengths $r$ of the $M$-regular sequences $f_1,\dots,f_r$ in $\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. So it suffices to show $r\le\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)$ for every such sequence; this is the claim $P(r)$ of Step 2 applied to $N=M$. (This is the case $IM
eq M$ of Lemma 00LJ, lemma-depth-weak-sequence, which the source invokes here.)

proof.text:
(The claim and its base case.) For $r\ge0$ let $P(r)$ be: for every nonzero finite $R$-module $N$ and every $N$-regular sequence $f_1,\dots,f_r$ in $\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(N)\ge r$, with $\dim\operatorname{Supp}$ the chain-length supremum of the statement. We prove $P(r)$ by induction on $r$. Base $r=0$: $N
eq0$, so $1
otin\operatorname{Ann}_R(N)$ and $\operatorname{Ann}_R(N)$ is a proper ideal; it lies in a maximal ideal (a maximal element, which exists as $R$ is Noetherian, of the proper ideals containing it), which is $\mathfrak m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-support-annihilator] $\operatorname{Supp}(N)=V(\operatorname{Ann}_R(N))
i\mathfrak m$, so the one-term chain $\mathfrak p_0=\mathfrak m$ lies in $\operatorname{Supp}(N)$ and $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(N)\ge0$. (The source: 'We may assume $d>0$ otherwise the lemma holds'.)

proof.text:
(Passing to $N/f_1N$.) Let $r\ge1$, $N
eq0$ finite and $f_1,\dots,f_r$ an $N$-regular sequence in $\mathfrak m$. Put $N'=N/f_1N$, a finite $R$-module. For $2\le i\le r+1$ the submodule $(f_2,\dots,f_{i-1})N'$ of $N'$ is the image of $(f_1,\dots,f_{i-1})N$, so $N'/(f_2,\dots,f_{i-1})N'\cong N/(f_1,\dots,f_{i-1})N$ as $R$-modules (third isomorphism theorem). Hence condition (1) of [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] for $f_2,\dots,f_r$ on $N'$ is condition (1) for $f_2,\dots,f_r$ on $N$, and $N'/(f_2,\dots,f_r)N'\cong N/(f_1,\dots,f_r)N
eq0$ is condition (2): $f_2,\dots,f_r$ is an $N'$-regular sequence in $\mathfrak m$ of length $r-1$. In particular $N'
eq0$, since it surjects onto $N/(f_1,\dots,f_r)N
eq0$. By the induction hypothesis $P(r-1)$, $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(N')\ge r-1$.

proof.text: (The dimension drops by exactly one; conclusion of the induction.) By condition (1) of [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] for $i=1$, $f_1\in\mathfrak m$ is a nonzerodivisor on $N$. By [lem-weil-pbc-support-dimension-quotient-element-equality], clause (2), applied to the finite module $N$ and $f=f_1$: $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(N/f_1N)+1=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(N)$. With Step 3, $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(N)=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(N')+1\ge(r-1)+1=r$ (if $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(N')=\infty$ then $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(N)=\infty\ge r$). This proves $P(r)$, hence $P(r)$ for all $r$ by induction.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00LK (lemma-bound-depth), proof lines 17829-17834 ('By Lemma lemma-one-equation-module we have dim(Supp(M/f_1M)) = dim(Supp(M)) - 1'), Lemma 0B52 (lemma-one-equation-module)

proof.text: (Conclusion.) By Step 1, $\operatorname{depth}(M)$ is the supremum of the lengths $r$ of $M$-regular sequences in $\mathfrak m$; by $P(r)$ (Steps 2-4) with $N=M\neq0$, each such $r$ satisfies $r\le\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)$. A supremum of numbers each $\le\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)$ is $\le\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)$, so $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)\ge\operatorname{depth}(M)$.
